text: Spatio-Temporal model (Marhuenda, Molina, & Morales, 2013) combines spatial correlation temporal autoregression DD areas TT time periods. panel need complete: cells without direct estimate predicted (see ). ydt=xdt⊤β+u1d+u2dt+edty_{dt} = x_{dt}^\top \beta + u_{1d} + u_{2dt} + e_{dt} : - u1=(u11,…,u1D)⊤u_1 = (u_{11}, \dots, u_{1D})^\top captures static spatial effects: u1=ρ1Wu1+ϵ1u_1 = \rho_1 W u_1 + \epsilon_1. - u2d=(u2d1,…,u2dT)⊤u_{2d} = (u_{2d1}, \dots, u_{2dT})^\top captures dynamic temporal effects area dd: u2dt=ρ2u2d,t−1+ϵ2dtu_{2dt} = \rho_2 u_{2d,t-1} + \epsilon_{2dt}. - edt∼ind. N(0,Ddt)e_{dt} \sim \text{ind. } N(0, D_{dt}) sampling errors. model defined full D×TD \times T grid: u1u_1 domains WW, u2u_2 periods.

title: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Models
text: addition frequentist C++ EBLUP implementations (eblup_sfh eblup_stfh), fastsae provides hb_area() Bayesian spatio-temporal modeling powered INLA. supports: - Bounded proportions via Beta regression (matching tipsae) - Discrete counts via Poisson Negative Binomial regression - Binary aggregates via Binomial regression - Flexible space-time structures including domain-specific random walks, separable dynamic fields, Knorr-Held Types –IV. full details case study Italian poverty data, see vignette Bayesian Area-Level Small Area Estimation INLA.

title: Sub-Area Level Estimation with Two-Fold Models
text: sub-area jj (j=1,…,Nij = 1, \dots, N_i) area ii (=1,…,mi = 1, \dots, m), direct estimator yijy_{ij} known sampling variance ψij\psi_{ij} follows yij=θij+eij,θij=xij⊤β+vi+uij,y_{ij} = \theta_{ij} + e_{ij}, \qquad \theta_{ij} = x_{ij}^\top \beta + v_i + u_{ij}, vi∼N(0,σv2)v_i \sim N(0, \sigma_v^2) area effect, uij∼N(0,σu2)u_{ij} \sim N(0, \sigma_u^2) sub-area effect eij∼N(0,ψij)e_{ij} \sim N(0, \psi_{ij}) sampling error, independent. Compared Fay-Herriot model, treats every sub-area unrelated, area effect viv_i estimated sampled sub-areas area ii. matters sub-areas sampled: get xij⊤β̂+v̂ix_{ij}^\top \hat\beta + \hat v_i instead synthetic xij⊤β̂x_{ij}^\top \hat\beta alone. sub-area area without sample predicted synthetically. output follows notation : random_effect_var holds sigma2_v (area) sigma2_u (sub-area), df_eblup (df_hb) holds random_effect_area random_effect_subarea.

title: Sub-Area Level Estimation with Two-Fold Models
text: simulate 30 areas 3 6 sub-areas , true sub-area means θij\theta_{ij} known. Fifteen sub-areas sample (direct estimate NA), sub-areas area A30 unsampled. row one sub-area. Unsampled sub-areas stay data y = NA covariates, predicted.
code: library(fastsae)  set.seed(2024) m <- 30 dat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(m), function(i) {   ni <- sample(3:6, 1)   data.frame(     area = sprintf("A%02d", i),     subarea = sprintf("A%02d-%d", i, seq_len(ni)),     x1 = rnorm(ni, mean = 2),     pop = sample(200:2000, ni)   ) })) v <- rnorm(m, sd = 1) names(v) <- unique(dat$area) dat$theta <- 10 + 2 * dat$x1 + v[dat$area] + rnorm(nrow(dat), sd = sqrt(0.5)) dat$vardir <- runif(nrow(dat), 0.5, 2) dat$y <- dat$theta + rnorm(nrow(dat), sd = sqrt(dat$vardir))  # Unsampled sub-areas: 15 at random, plus every sub-area of A30 unsampled <- union(sample(which(dat$area != "A30"), 15), which(dat$area == "A30")) dat$y[unsampled] <- NA  c(subareas = nrow(dat), sampled = sum(!is.na(dat$y))) #> subareas  sampled  #>      131      111 head(dat) #>   area subarea        x1  pop    theta   vardir        y #> 1  A01   A01-1 1.5347257 1857 13.78128 1.663801 12.20118 #> 2  A01   A01-2 2.5191534 1961 15.03099 1.105026 14.48113 #> 3  A01   A01-3 2.5284898 1222 14.79953 1.301555 15.01471 #> 4  A01   A01-4 1.4848072 1252 11.84648 1.406429 11.36094 #> 5  A02   A02-1 1.8729653 1255 13.61192 1.986447 12.02304 #> 6  A02   A02-2 0.7751246  924 12.23727 1.268523       NA

title: Unit-Level Estimation with Battese-Harter-Fuller
text: Unlike area-level models aggregate data prior modeling, unit-level models operate directly individual survey unit records (e.g., households, farms, persons) linking population auxiliary aggregates (e.g., census means satellite imagery). fastsae package implements nested error regression model Battese, Harter, Fuller (1988) via eblup_bhf(), providing fast estimation parallel parametric bootstrap MSE. hb_unit() fits model hierarchical Bayes model INLA (see last section).

title: Unit-Level Estimation with Battese-Harter-Fuller
text: individual unit jj (j=1,…,ndj = 1, \dots, n_d) small area dd (d=1,…,Dd = 1, \dots, D): ydj=xdj⊤β+ud+edjy_{dj} = x_{dj}^\top \beta + u_d + e_{dj} : - ud∼..d. N(0,σu2)u_d \sim \text{..d. } N(0, \sigma_u^2) area-specific random effect. - edj∼..d. N(0,σe2)e_{dj} \sim \text{..d. } N(0, \sigma_e^2) unit-level error variance. - udu_d edje_{dj} mutually independent. small area population mean Y‾d\bar{Y}_d estimated : Y‾̂dEBLUP=X‾d⊤β̂+γd(y‾d−x‾d⊤β̂)\hat{\bar{Y}}_d^{\text{EBLUP}} = \bar{X}_d^\top \hat{\beta} + \gamma_d (\bar{y}_d - \bar{x}_d^\top \hat{\beta}) : - X‾d\bar{X}_d known population mean vector auxiliary variables domain dd. - y‾d\bar{y}_d x‾d\bar{x}_d sample means domain dd. - γd=σu2σu2+σe2/nd\gamma_d = \frac{\sigma_u^2}{\sigma_u^2 + \sigma_e^2 / n_d} shrinkage ratio.

what: Understanding INLA: Fast Bayesian Inference without MCMC
title: High-Performance Frequentist and Bayesian Small Area Estimation
text: INLA (Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations; Rue et al., 2009) provides deterministic alternative Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) Bayesian inference latent Gaussian models. Instead drawing thousands samples, INLA: Approximates posterior marginals analytically using Laplace approximations Integrates non-Gaussian observations analytically Delivers results seconds rather hours fastsae uses INLA INLA R package fit hierarchical Bayesian small area models : 6 likelihood families: Gaussian, Beta, Binomial, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gamma Spatial random effects: Besag ICAR, BYM, BYM2, Leroux, SAR, spatial lag Temporal random effects: RW1, RW2, AR(1) Spatio-temporal interactions: separable non-separable structures Compared MCMC: chains run monitor, deterministic results, fits seconds. INLA approximation: fastsae chose settings comparing exact posteriors long Stan runs, engine = jax_engine() fits models MCMC check needed.

what: Benchmark Small Area Estimation Predictions to Aggregate Targets — benchmark_sae
title: Benchmark Small Area Estimation Predictions to Aggregate Targets — benchmark_sae
text: Calibrates small area model predictions (hb_area, eblup_fh, eblup_sfh, eblup_stfh, eblup_bhf) weighted aggregate matches known benchmark targets higher administrative levels (e.g. provincial national totals/means), required official statistics production. Supports: Single-Stage Benchmarking: Calibrates small areas directly aggregate target     (either globally within sub-regions/provinces via group). Two-Stage Hierarchical Benchmarking (Rao Molina, 2015, Sec 10.4; spirit Ghosh Steorts, 2013):     Calibrates small areas (e.g. 500 Kabupaten/Kota) within overarching groups (e.g. 34 Provinces)     simultaneously harmonizing provincial aggregates match overarching National Target     (national_target). Guarantees simultaneous mathematical consistency across administrative tiers:     \(\sum_{d \\text{Prov}_g} \tilde{w}_{dg} \hat{\theta}_{dg}^{\text{BM}} = T_g^*\)     \(\sum_g \tilde{W}_g T_g^* = T_{\text{nat}}\). Methods implemented: "ratio": Proportional / multiplicative adjustment. Preserves area proportions non-negativity (Rao Molina, 2015). "difference": Uniform additive adjustment (Rao Molina, 2015, Section 10.3). "optimal": Variance-weighted quadratic loss benchmarking (Datta et al., 2011; Bell, Datta Ghosh, 2013).     Domains higher MSE absorb larger adjustments precise domains remain minimally perturbed. "logit": Logit-scale additive shift bounded indicators \(\theta_d \(0, 1)\): one shift per group logit scale, benchmarked estimates stay (0, 1).

what: Compare Two Small Area Estimation Models — compare_sae
title: Compare Two Small Area Estimation Models — compare_sae
text: Provides comprehensive evaluation concordance comparison two fitted Small Area Estimation (SAE) models (e.g. comparing Classical Fay-Herriot vs Spatial Fay-Herriot, Area-level vs Unit-level BHF, EBLUP vs HB). Computes agreement, ranking efficiency metrics: Agreement estimates (Bland Altman 1986): mean difference     \(\bar d\) Model 2 minus Model 1, 95% limits agreement     \(\bar d \pm 1.96\, s_d\), mean absolute difference (MAE) root mean     squared difference (RMSD), Lin's (1989) concordance correlation coefficient     \(\rho_c = 2 s_{12} / (s_1^2 + s_2^2 + (\bar\theta_1 - \bar\theta_2)^2)\) (moments     divisor \(n\)), 1 estimates lie identity line. Differences relative uncertainty: \(z_d = (\hat\theta_{2d} -     \hat\theta_{1d}) / \sqrt{\text{MSE}_{1d}}\), summarised median absolute value     share domains \(|z_d| > 1\). descriptive, test:     estimators use data, difference smaller variance either. Ranking domains: Spearman's rank correlation, mean absolute change     rank, share top highest lowest domains Model 1     also among highest lowest Model 2 (domains programme target). Efficiency: mean median MSE ratio (\(\text{MSE}_1 / \text{MSE}_2\)),     share domains Model 2 lower MSE, mean RSE (%) model. Pearson's correlation reported: two reasonable models data correlate almost perfectly whatever differences, correlation measures association, agreement (model 10% higher everywhere still \(r = 1\); Bland Altman 1986).

title: Create Spatial Proximity and Weights Matrix — create_weights
text: data sf polygon point object, numeric matrix data frame 2D coordinates (columns x/y longitude/latitude), spdep nb listw object. method Character string specifying spatial weight method: "queen": Queen contiguity (sharing least one vertex boundary edge). "rook": Rook contiguity (sharing common linear boundary edge). "knn": \(k\)-nearest neighbors based centroid/point distances. "distance": Distance band domains within d_max neighbors. "idw": Inverse distance weighting \(w_{ij} = 1 / d_{ij}^\alpha\). style Character string specifying normalization style: "W": Row-standardized (row sums equal 1, default SAR/SFH models). "B": Binary adjacency (0/1 values, standard INLA BYM2/Besag models). "C": Globally standardized. "U": Equal weighting (\(1 / m\)). "minmax": Min-max spectral normalization (divided largest eigenvalue). k Integer. Number nearest neighbors method = "knn" (default 4). d_max Numeric. Distance threshold method = "distance". NULL, automatically set minimum distance ensuring disconnected domains. alpha Numeric. Distance decay power method = "idw" (default 1). island_fallback Logical. TRUE (default), disconnected domains islands zero contiguous neighbors automatically connected nearest neighbor(s) based centroid distance. k_fallback Integer. Number nearest neighbors connect isolated islands island_fallback = TRUE (default 1). domain Optional vector, column name, one-sided formula referencing domain IDs. provided, used row column names resulting matrix.

title: Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction based on a Spatio-Temporal Fay-Herriot Model. — eblup_stfh
text: function gives Spatio-Temporal Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (EBLUP) normality based spatio-temporal Fay-Herriot model. reimplements Fisher-scoring algorithm eblupSTFH() (package sae, Marhuenda, Molina & Morales 2013), estimation loop runs compiled C++/Armadillo, making substantially faster memory-efficient original R implementation – especially large number domains/time periods.

title: Generalized Variance Function (GVF) Smoothing for Sampling Variances — gvf_smooth
text: vardir vector, column name, one-sided formula referencing direct sampling variances data. y optional vector, column name, one-sided formula referencing direct survey estimates. n optional vector, column name, one-sided formula referencing domain sample sizes. method character string specifying GVF smoothing model: "log_linear" Log-linear model: \(\log(D_i) = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1 \log(y_i) + \alpha_2 \log(n_i) + \varepsilon_i\). Includes second-order bias correction upon exponentiation. "gamma_glm" Gamma GLM log link: \(\mathrm{E}[D_i] = \mu_i, \log(\mu_i) = \alpha_0 + \dots\). Naturally suited strictly positive variances without back-transformation bias. "cv_power" Power model direct coefficients variation: \(\log(CV_i^2) = \alpha_0 + \dots\). Default "log_linear". data optional data frame containing variables. formula optional user-supplied formula overriding default model specification. bias_correction logical. "log_linear", whether apply log-normal bias correction \(\tilde{D}_i = \exp(\hat{\mu}_i + \hat{\sigma}^2 / 2)\). Default TRUE.

"binomial": Binary / proportion response. Requires trials. "poisson": Count response / disease rate. Supports exposure. "nbinomial": Negative Binomial overdispersed counts. vardir     provided, size area fixed \(V_i = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/n_i\)     \(n_i = \hat\mu_i^2/(V_i - \hat\mu_i)\) (near-Poisson size     \(V_i \le \hat\mu_i\)), \(\hat\mu_i\) posterior mean first fit     estimates one size (model fitted twice); without vardir     common size weakly identified area effect (warning). "beta": Continuous proportions strictly (0, 1). vardir     provided, precision area fixed     \(V_i = \mu_i(1 - \mu_i)/(\phi_i + 1)\)     \(\phi_i = \hat\mu_i(1 - \hat\mu_i)/V_i - 1\) (least 1), \(\hat\mu_i\)     posterior mean first fit precision direct estimate     \(y_i\) (Janicki 2020), model fitted twice. trials     provided instead, precision \(n_i - 1\) (simple random sampling; give     effective sample sizes complex designs); , trials ignored     (warning). Without either, one precision estimated, weakly     identified area effect. "gamma": Skewed positive continuous response. vardir     provided, precision area scaled \(y_i^2 / V_i\); without     precision estimated one observation per area, weakly     identified area effect (warning; INLA 95% intervals     covered 83-88% true means simulation, 91-95% vardir). spatial Character string specifying spatial random effect structure: "none": Non-spatial IID area random intercept (default). "bym2": Scaled Besag-York-Mollié 2 model (Riebler et al., 2016),     decomposing area variance spatial (\(\phi\)) unstructured components. "bym": Classic Besag-York-Mollié (1991) model. "besag": Intrinsic Conditional Autoregressive (ICAR) model. "generic1": Leroux spatial autoregressive model. "sar": Simultaneous autoregressive (SAR) area effect,     \(\eta = X\beta + u\), \(u = (- \rho W)^{-1}\epsilon\),     \(\epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2 )\): model eblup_sfh     (Petrucci Salvati, 2006), \(\rho\) uniform \(|\rho| \le 0.999\).     INLA "slm" latent model zero covariate matrix,     \(\epsilon\) filtered. combinable "type3",     "type4" "separable" interactions, CAR fields. Note covariates spatially filtered ,     Bayesian counterpart eblup_sfh, whose SAR     structure applies random effect : \(X\beta + (- \rho W)^{-1}\epsilon\). "rw1": First-order random walk across time periods. "rw2": Second-order random walk across time periods. "ar1": First-order autoregressive process across time periods. what: Unified Spatial Choropleth Mapping for Small Area Estimates — map_sae
title: Unified Spatial Choropleth Mapping for Small Area Estimates — map_sae
text: Provides comprehensive, single-gateway spatial choropleth mapping interface Small Area Estimation models fitted fastsae (e.g. eblup_fh, eblup_sfh, eblup_stfh, eblup_bhf, hb_area, benchmark_sae). Intelligently handles: Single Model Visualizations: Point estimates ("estimate"), Relative     Standard Error ("rse"), 3-color official statistics reliability classification     ("reliability": green reliable, amber use caution, red unreliable; cut-offs     thresholds, see add_reliability_flags). Direct vs Model Comparisons: Side--side facet maps contrasting erratic direct survey     estimates smoothed small area model estimates ("comparison"). Two-Model Comparisons: Side--side maps spatial difference maps ("difference")     contrasting two competing models (e.g. Classical FH vs Spatial FH, FastSAE vs Stan). Benchmarked Calibrations: Visualizing pre- vs post-benchmarked calibrations. Smart Key Matching: Automatically detects common domain identifier     model sf_geom, optional manual override via key.

title: Unified Spatial Choropleth Mapping for Small Area Estimates — map_sae
code: map_sae(object, ...)  # S3 method for class 'fastsae' map_sae(   object,   model2 = NULL,   sf_geom = NULL,   key = NULL,   type = c("estimate", "rse", "reliability", "comparison", "difference"),   indicator = NULL,   palette = NULL,   thresholds = c(25, 50),   facet_scales = "fixed",   title = NULL,   subtitle = NULL,   ... )  # S3 method for class 'fastsae_benchmark' map_sae(   object,   sf_geom = NULL,   key = NULL,   type = c("comparison", "estimate", "difference"),   indicator = NULL,   palette = NULL,   title = NULL,   subtitle = NULL,   ... )  # S3 method for class 'list' map_sae(   object,   sf_geom = NULL,   key = NULL,   type = c("comparison", "difference"),   indicator = NULL,   palette = NULL,   title = NULL,   subtitle = NULL,   ... )  # Default S3 method map_sae(   object,   sf_geom = NULL,   key = NULL,   type = c("estimate", "rse", "reliability"),   indicator = NULL,   palette = NULL,   thresholds = c(25, 50),   title = NULL,   subtitle = NULL,   ... )

title: Unified Spatial Choropleth Mapping for Small Area Estimates — map_sae
text: object fitted fastsae model object, fastsae_benchmark object, named list fastsae objects, data frame containing domain estimates. ... Additional arguments passed ggplot2 layers. model2 Optional second fastsae model object direct model--model comparison. sf_geom Spatial polygon geometry class sf. Optional model fitted data already inherits sf. key Optional character string named vector specifying column(s) used match model domain identifiers spatial geometry sf_geom. NULL (default), automatically detects matching key evaluating     common column names highest set intersection overlap domain IDs sf_geom columns. single string (e.g. key = "kd_kab"), specifies column sf_geom     match model domain IDs. named string (e.g. key = c("domain" = "kd_kab")), explicitly pairs model's     domain column spatial column sf_geom. type Character string specifying visualization type: "estimate": Choropleth map small area point estimates (HB EBLUP). "rse": Choropleth map Relative Standard Errors / CV (%). "reliability": 3-color traffic light map reliability tiers     (default RSE \(\le 25\%\) reliable, 25–50% use caution, \(> 50\%\) unreliable). "comparison": Side--side facet choropleth map (Direct vs Model, Model 1 vs Model 2). "difference": Spatial difference map (\(\hat{\theta}^{(2)} - \hat{\theta}^{(1)}\)     \(\hat{\theta}^{\text{Model}} - \hat{\theta}^{\text{Direct}}\)) divergent color palette. indicator Optional alias type. supplied, overrides type. palette Character string specifying color palette. Default automatically selected based type: "viridis" estimates, "magma" RSE, official traffic-light colors reliability, "RdBu" / "PuOr" differences. thresholds Numeric vector length 2 defining RSE (%) thresholds reliability classification (see add_reliability_flags). Default c(25, 50), BPS-Statistics Indonesia criteria. facet_scales Character string passed ggplot2::facet_wrap(scales = ...). Default "fixed". title Optional title plot. NULL, descriptive title generated automatically. subtitle Optional subtitle plot.
